title: Your First Program
description: Every word in a C++ program explained, line by line, so none of it is magic.

content.value: Here is a complete C++ program. It prints one line. Every program you write starts from this shape, so it is worth taking apart.

parts.label: paste in
parts.note: An instruction for the preprocessor: copy in a part of the library.

parts.label: which part
parts.note: Input/output stream: the part of the **standard library** (ready-made code that comes with C++) for printing and reading.

content.title: Line 1: bring in the printing tools
content.caption: Without this line the compiler has never heard of `cout`.

content.text: The standard library keeps its names inside a **namespace** called `std` (short for standard). The screen's full name is really `std::cout`.

items.title: Short names
items.text: Line 2 says "also look in `std`", so `cout` is enough.

items.title: Full names
items.text: Leave line 2 out and write `std::` in front of each name.

content.title: Two ways to write the same thing
content.caption: Big projects often write `std::` every time to avoid name clashes. This course uses the short style, and now you can read both.

content.question: You leave out `using namespace std;`. How do you write `cout`?
content.explain: Without that line, you write the full name: the namespace `std`, then `::`, then `cout`.

parts.label: hands back a number
parts.note: When `main` finishes, it returns a whole number.

parts.label: open
parts.note: Opens the function. Its matching `}` closes it.

content.value: The last line inside, `return 0;`, hands 0 back to whoever started the program. 0 means "finished with no problems".
Misspell `main` and the build fails with an `undefined reference` error. Nothing told the computer where to begin.
content.title: The name matters

content.question: When your program starts, where does it begin?
options: At the very first line of the file
content.explain: Every C++ program begins running at the function called `main`.

content.value: Line 5 is the only line that does visible work. Everything else is the wrapper around it.

parts.label: goes into
parts.note: Sends what is on its right into `cout`.

parts.label: text
parts.note: Double quotes mark where the text starts and ends.

parts.label: end the line
parts.note: Moves the output to a new line.

content.title: Line 5: print something
content.caption: Whenever you see `<<` next to `cout`, think "goes into".

content.question: What does this print?
content.explain: The quotes only mark where the text starts and ends. `cout` prints what is inside them.

items: Every `{` needs a matching `}`. Here only `main` opens a pair, so the program ends with one `}`.
Indent inner lines four spaces. C++ doesn't require it, but it shows what is inside what.
Your code lives in `main.cpp`. Any name ending in `.cpp` works, but a program has exactly one `main`.
content.title: Rules to keep

steps.note: `{` opens `main`. The program starts running here.
The last `}` closes `main`. The program ends.

content.title: Braces in pairs
content.outro: Try it: add a third `cout` line between the others. It prints exactly where you put it, because instructions run top to bottom.

content.question: How many `}` does this one-line program end with?
content.explain: Only `main` opens a pair of braces, so one `}` closes it.

practice.question: Print your own name on one line, then your favourite food on a second line. Two instructions inside `main`.
Print a three line message: C++ is strict. / Braces come in pairs. / And I am fine with that. Each on its own line.

quiz.question: Where does a C++ program start running?
options: At the first line of the file.
quiz.explain: The program begins at `main`, found by name. That is why the spelling of `main` matters so much.

quiz.question: What does `using namespace std;` let you do?
options: Skip the semicolons in your program.
quiz.explain: Standard names live in the `std` namespace. The line lets you use their short names; you still need the `#include` to bring the tools in.

quiz.question: What does `endl` do?
options: Ends the current line, so the next output starts underneath.
quiz.explain: `endl` is short for end line. Without it, the next thing you print carries on along the same line.

quiz.question: What does `return 0;` at the end of `main` mean?
options: The program finished with no problems.
Start the program again from the top.
quiz.explain: `main` hands a number back when it ends. By agreement, 0 means success and anything else means something went wrong.
